Q 46:20 · Vol. 4, pp. 305–306

Verse 20

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: “You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; so today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for having been arrogant in the earth without right and for having been defiantly disobedient” (20)
وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِها فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ (20)
Vol. 4, p. 305
The operator of the adverbial is the implied saying before “adhhabtum.” Their exposure to the Fire means their being tormented by it, from their saying “Banū so-and-so were exposed to the sword”(1) when they were killed by it. From it is His saying: “the Fire — they are exposed to it.” It is also possible that what is meant is the exposure of the Fire to them, from their saying “ʿaraḍtu l-nāqata ʿalā l-ḥawḍ” (“I presented the she-camel to the trough”), by which they mean presenting the trough to her, so they reversed it. This is indicated by the exegesis of Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ: they are brought to it and it is unveiled for them. “You squandered your good things”: that is, no share of good things was written for you except what you already obtained in your worldly life, and you have gone off with it and taken it; so nothing of it remains for you after you exhausted your share. From ʿUmar ؓ: “If I wished, I would call for thin breads (ṣalāʾiq), mustard-and-raisin sauce (ṣanāb), camel briskets (karākir) and humps;(2) but I saw that God Most High censured a people for their good things, saying: ‘You squandered your good things in your worldly life.’”(3) And from him: “If I wished I would be the best of you in food and the finest of you in clothing, but I am saving my good things.”(4) And from the Messenger of God ﷺ: he entered upon the People of the Bench (Ahl al-Ṣuffa) while they were patching their garments with scraps of leather, finding no [cloth] patches for them, and said: “Are you better today, or on the day
ناصب الظرف هو القول المضمر قبل أَذْهَبْتُمْ وعرضهم على النار: تعذيبهم بها، من قولهم: عرض بنو فلان على السيف «1» إذا قتلوا به. ومنه قوله تعالى النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها ويجوز أن يراد: عرض النار عليهم من قولهم: عرضت الناقة على الحوض، يريدون: عرض الحوض عليها فقلبوا. ويدل عليه تفسير ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: يجاء بهم إليها فيكشف لهم عنها أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ أى: ما كتب لكم حظ من الطيبات إلا ما قد أصبتموه في دنياكم، وقد ذهبتم به وأخذتموه، فلم يبق لكم بعد استيفاء حظكم شيء منها. وعن عمر رضى الله عنه: لو شئت لدعوت بصلائق وصناب «2» وكراكر وأسنمة، ولكنى رأيت الله تعالى نعى على قوم طيباتهم فقال: أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا «3» . وعنه: لو شئت لكنت أطيبكم طعاما وأحسنكم لباسا، ولكنى أستبقى طيباتى: «4» وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه دخل على أهل الصفة وهم يرقعون ثيابهم بالأدم ما يجدون لها رقاعا، فقال: أأنتم اليوم خير أم يوم
Vol. 4, p. 306
when one of you goes out in the morning in one garment and in the evening in another, and a platter is brought to him in the morning and another in the evening, and his house is covered as the Kaʿba is covered?” They said: “We are better on that day.” He said: “Rather, you are better today.”(1) It is read “a-adhhabtum” with the interrogative hamza; and “ā-adhhabtum” with an alif between two hamzas. Al-hūn and al-hawān [are two forms of the word]; it is also read “ʿadhāb al-hawān.” And “tafsuqūna” is read with ḍamma and with kasra on the sīn.
يغدو أحدكم في حلة ويروح في أخرى، ويغدى عليه بجفنة ويراح عليه بأخرى، ويستر بيته كما تستر الكعبة. قالوا: نحن يومئذ خير. قال. بل أنتم اليوم خير «1» وقرئ: أذهبتم بهمزة الاستفهام. وآ أذهبتم بألف بين همزتين، الهون. والهوان: وقرئ عذاب الهوان، وقرئ يفسقون بضم السين وكسرها.

Vol. 4, p. 306
1. (1) . Recorded by al-Ṭabarī from the narration of Saʿd from Qatāda, who said: “It was mentioned to us,” and he mentioned it. And [it came] by his route from al-Shaʿbī. Abū Nuʿaym narrated it in al-Ḥilya, in the biography of the People of the Bench, from the route of al-Ḥasan, who said: “ḥasb aḍʿāf al-muslimīn” [the printed words are unclear], and he mentioned something like it at length. And in al-Tirmidhī, from the route of Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī: “Someone who heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib ؓ told me: While we were sitting in the mosque, Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr came upon us, wearing only a cloak of his, patched with fur. When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw him, he wept for the comfort that [Muṣʿab] had been in. Then he said: ‘How will you be …’” — the ḥadīth, similar to it.
1. (1) . أخرجه الطبري من رواية سعد عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا. فذكره. ومن طريقه الشعبي. ورواه أبو نعيم في الحلية في ترجمة أهل الصفة من طريق الحسن قال «حسب أضعاف المسلمين» فذكر نحوه مطولا وفي الترمذي من طريق محمد بن كعب القرظي: حدثني من سمع على بن أبى طالب رضى الله عنه قال: بينا نحن جلوس في المسجد إذ طلع علينا مصعب بن عمير ما عليه إلا بردة له مرقوعة بفرو. فلما رآه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكى للذي كان فيه من النعمة. ثم قال: كيف بكم
…. الحديث نحوه» .

Q 46:21 · Vol. 4, p. 306

Verse 21

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And mention the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people at al-Aḥqāf — and warners had passed before him and after him — “Worship none but God. Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a mighty day” (21)
وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوا إِلاَّ اللَّهَ إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ (21)
Vol. 4, p. 306
Al-Aḥqāf: plural of ḥiqf, a long, elevated sand dune with a curve in it, from iḥqawqafa l-shayʾ, when a thing bends. ʿĀd were people of pillars, who dwelt among sands overlooking the sea, in a land called al-Shiḥr, of the lands of Yemen. It is said: between ʿUmān and Mahra. Al-nudhur is the plural of nadhīr, in the sense of mundhir (“warner”) or of indhār (“warning”). “from before him” means before him, and “and from behind him” means after him. It is also read “from before him and from after him.” The meaning: Hūd ﷺ had warned them, saying to them: “Worship none but God; I fear for you the punishment,” and he informed them that the messengers sent before him and those who would be sent after him are all warners like his warning. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ: he means the messengers who were sent before him and those who were sent in his time. The meaning of “and from behind him” on this exegesis is “and after his warning.” This holds if you connect “warners had passed” with His saying “he warned his people.” But you may also make His saying “and warners had passed before him and after him” a parenthetical interjection between “he warned his people” and “that you not worship,” in which case the meaning would be: and mention Hūd’s warning his people of the consequence of polytheism and of the mighty punishment, while the messengers before him and after him warned likewise; so remind them.
الأحقاف: جمع حقف وهو رمل مستطيل مرتفع فيه انحناء، من احقوقف الشيء إذا اعوج، وكانت عاد أصحاب عمد يسكنون بين رمال مشرفين على البحر بأرض يقال لها الشحر من بلاد اليمن. وقيل: بين عمان ومهرة. والنُّذُرُ جمع نذير بمعنى المنذر أو الإنذار مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ من قبله وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ ومن بعده. وقرئ: من بين يديه ومن بعده. والمعنى: أنّ هودا عليه السلام قد أنذرهم فقال لهم: لا تعبدوا إلا الله إنى أخاف عليكم العذاب، وأعلمهم أنّ الرسل الذين بعثوا قبله والذين سيبعثون بعده كلهم منذرون نحو إنذاره وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: يعنى الرسل الذين بعثوا قبله والذين بعثوا في زمانه. ومعنى وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ على هذا التفسير ومن بعد إنذاره، هذا إذا علقت، وقد خلت النذر بقوله: أنذر قومه، ولك أن تجعل قوله تعالى وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ اعتراضا بين أنذر قومه وبين أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا ويكون المعنى: واذكر إنذار هود قومه عاقبة الشرك والعذاب العظيم وقد أنذر من تقدمه من الرسل ومن تأخر عنه مثل ذلك، فاذكرهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 306
1. (1) . Recorded by al-Ṭabarī from the narration of Saʿd from Qatāda, who said: “It was mentioned to us,” and he mentioned it. And [it came] by his route from al-Shaʿbī. Abū Nuʿaym narrated it in al-Ḥilya, in the biography of the People of the Bench, from the route of al-Ḥasan, who said: “ḥasb aḍʿāf al-muslimīn” [the printed words are unclear], and he mentioned something like it at length. And in al-Tirmidhī, from the route of Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī: “Someone who heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib ؓ told me: While we were sitting in the mosque, Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr came upon us, wearing only a cloak of his, patched with fur. When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw him, he wept for the comfort that [Muṣʿab] had been in. Then he said: ‘How will you be …’” — the ḥadīth, similar to it.
1. (1) . أخرجه الطبري من رواية سعد عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا. فذكره. ومن طريقه الشعبي. ورواه أبو نعيم في الحلية في ترجمة أهل الصفة من طريق الحسن قال «حسب أضعاف المسلمين» فذكر نحوه مطولا وفي الترمذي من طريق محمد بن كعب القرظي: حدثني من سمع على بن أبى طالب رضى الله عنه قال: بينا نحن جلوس في المسجد إذ طلع علينا مصعب بن عمير ما عليه إلا بردة له مرقوعة بفرو. فلما رآه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكى للذي كان فيه من النعمة. ثم قال: كيف بكم
…. الحديث نحوه» .

Q 46:22 · Vol. 4, p. 306

Verse 22

The verse as the commentary quotes it
They said: “Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful” (22)
قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا لِتَأْفِكَنا عَنْ آلِهَتِنا فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (22)
Vol. 4, p. 306
Al-ifk: turning away. One says: afakahu ʿan raʾyihi (“he turned him from his opinion”). “from our gods”: from worshipping them. “what you threaten us with”: of hastening the punishment for polytheism. “If you are” truthful in your threat.
الإفك: الصرف. يقال أفكه عن رأيه عَنْ آلِهَتِنا عن عبادتها بِما تَعِدُنا من معاجلة العذاب على الشرك إِنْ كُنْتَ صادقا في وعدك.

Q 46:23 · Vol. 4, pp. 306–307

Verse 23

The verse as the commentary quotes it
He said: “The knowledge is only with God, and I convey to you that with which I was sent; but I see you to be a people who are ignorant” (23)
قالَ إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وَلكِنِّي أَراكُمْ قَوْماً تَجْهَلُونَ (23)
Vol. 4, p. 306
If you say: in what way does His saying “The knowledge is only with God” fit as an answer to their saying “Then bring us what you threaten us with”?
فإن قلت: من أين طابق قوله تعالى إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ جوابا لقولهم فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا؟
Vol. 4, p. 307
I say: in that this saying of theirs is a request for hastening the punishment. Do you not see His saying: “Rather, it is what you sought to hasten”? So he said to them: I have no knowledge of the time at which your punishment would be wise and proper; that knowledge is only with God. So how could I ask Him to bring His punishment upon you at a hasty time that you yourselves propose? And the meaning of “and I convey to you what I was sent with” — it is also read with takhfīf [“ublighukum”] — is that what is my business and my condition is that I convey to you, to the best of my effort, what I was sent with of warning, frightening, and turning away from whatever exposes you to God’s wrath. “But you are ignorant”: you do not know that the messengers were sent only as warners, not as those who propose [signs], nor as askers for anything other than what they have been permitted.
قلت: من حيث إنّ قولهم هذا استعجال منهم بالعذاب. ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ فقال لهم: لا علم عندي بالوقت الذي يكون فيه تعذيبكم حكمة وصوابا، إنما علم ذلك عند الله، فكيف أدعوه بأن يأتيكم بعذابه في وقت عاجل تقترحونه أنتم؟ ومعنى: وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وقرئ بالتخفيف: أن الذي هو شأنى وشرطي: أن أبلغكم ما أرسلت به من الإنذار والتخويف والصرف عما يعرّضكم لسخط الله بجهدي، ولكنكم جاهلون لا تعلمون أنّ الرسل لم يبعثوا إلا منذرين لا مقترحين، ولا سائلين غير ما أذن لهم فيه.

Q 46:24–25 · Vol. 4, pp. 307–308

Verses 24 to 25

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Then when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: “This is a cloud bringing us rain.” “Rather, it is that which you sought to hasten — a wind in which is a painful punishment (24), destroying everything by the command of its Lord.” So they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people (25)
فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عارِضاً مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قالُوا هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيها عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (24) تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّها فَأَصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إِلاَّ مَساكِنُهُمْ كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (25)
Vol. 4, p. 307
“Then when they saw it”: there are two possibilities for the pronoun. It may refer back to “what you threaten us with”; or it may be indefinite, its matter made clear by His saying “ʿāriḍan,” either as a specification (tamyīz) or as a ḥāl. This second analysis is clearer and more eloquent. Al-ʿāriḍ is the cloud that spreads across the horizon of the sky. Like it are al-ḥabā and al-ʿanān, from ḥabā and ʿanna when something appears. The annexation of “mustaqbil” and “mumṭir” is figurative, not definite, as is shown by their occurring, though annexed to two definite nouns, as descriptions of an indefinite noun. “Rather, it is”: before it there is an implied saying, and the speaker is Hūd ﷺ; the evidence for it is the reading of one who read “Hūd said: Nay, it is …” It is also read “Say: Nay, it is what you sought to hasten, it is a wind,” i.e., God Almighty said: Say. “destroying everything”: it destroys of the persons of ʿĀd and their possessions a great mass; so He expressed abundance by totality. It is also read “yudammiru kulla shayʾ,” from damara dimāran, when one perishes. “you will not see”: the address is to whoever sees, whoever he may be. It is also read “lā yurā,” in the passive, with yāʾ and with tāʾ. The interpretation of the reading with tāʾ, which is from al-Ḥasan ؓ is: you will not see any survivors or any things of theirs except their dwellings. From it is the verse of Dhū l-Rumma: “and nothing remained but the bulging ribs” — and it is not strong. It is also read “lā tarā illā maskanahum” and “lā yurā illā maskanuhum.” It is related that the wind would carry the tent and the woman in her howdah and lift them into the air until they were seen like a locust. It is said: the first to see the punishment was a woman of theirs, who said: “I saw a wind in which was something like sparks of fire.” It is related: the first thing by which they knew that it was a punishment was that they saw what was in the desert of their saddles and livestock being carried by the wind between sky and earth; so they entered their houses and closed their doors, and the wind tore off
فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ في الضمير وجهان: أن يرجع إلى ما تعدنا، وأن يكون مبهما قد وضح أمره بقوله عارِضاً إما تمييزا وإما حالا. وهذا الوجه أعرب وأفصح. والعارض: السحاب الذي يعرض في أفق السماء. ومثله: الحبى والعنان، من حبا وعنّ: إذا عرض. وإضافة مستقبل وممطر مجازية غير معرفة بدليل وقوعهما وهما مضافان إلى معرفتين وصفا للنكرة بَلْ هُوَ القول قبله مضمر، والقائل: هود عليه السلام، والدليل عليه قراءة من قرأ: قال هود، بل هو. وقرئ: قل بل ما استعجلتم به هي ريح، أى قال الله تعالى: قل تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ تهلك من نفوس عاد وأموالهم الجم الكثير، فعبر عن الكثرة بالكلية. وقرئ يدمر كل شيء من دمر دمارا إذا هلك لا تَرى الخطاب للرائى من كان. وقرئ: لا يرى، على البناء للمفعول بالياء والتاء، وتأويل القراءة بالتاء وهي عن الحسن رضى الله عنه: لا ترى بقايا ولا أشياء منهم إلا مساكنهم. ومنه بيت ذى الرمّة: وما بقيت إلّا الضلوع الجراشع» وليست بالقوية. وقرئ: لا ترى إلا مسكنهم، ولا يرى إلا مسكنهم. وروى أنّ الريح كانت تحمل الفسطاط والظعينة فترفعها في الجوّ حتى ترى كأنها جرادة. وقيل: أوّل من أبصر العذاب امرأة منهم قالت: رأيت ريحا فيها كشهب النار. وروى: أوّل ما عرفوا به أنه عذاب: أنهم رأوا ما كان في الصحراء من رحالهم ومواشيهم تطير به الريح السماء والأرض، فدخلوا بيوتهم وغلقوا أبوابهم، فقلعت الريح
Vol. 4, p. 308
the doors and threw them down; and God piled the sand dunes (al-Aḥqāf) over them, so they were beneath them for seven nights and eight days, groaning; then the wind uncovered them, carried them and cast them into the sea. It is related that when Hūd sensed the wind, he drew a line around himself and the believers, beside a flowing spring. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both: Hūd and those with him withdrew into an enclosure; nothing of the wind touched them except what was gentle on the skin and pleasing to the souls, while it passed over ʿĀd carrying away their howdahs between heaven and earth and pelting them with stones. And from the Prophet ﷺ: when he saw wind, he would be alarmed and say: “O God, I ask You for its good and the good of what it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what it was sent with.”(1) And when he saw a rain-cloud he would stand and sit, come and go, and his color would change; so it was said to him: “O Messenger of God, what do you fear?” He would say: “I fear that it may be like the people of ʿĀd when they said: ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’”
الأبواب وصرعتهم، وأما الله عليهم الأحقاف فكانوا تحتها سبع ليال وثمانية أيام لهم أنين، ثم كشفت الريح عنهم، فاحتملتهم فطرحتهم في البحر. وروى أنّ هودا لما أحس بالريح خط على نفسه وعلى المؤمنين خطا إلى جنب عين تنبع. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: اعتزل هود ومن معه في حظيرة ما يصيبهم من الريح إلا مايلين على الجلود وتلذه الأنفس، وإنها لتمر من عاد بالظعن بين السماء والأرض وتدمغهم بالحجارة وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا رأى الريح فزع وقال: اللهم إنى أسألك خيرها وخير ما أرسلت به، وأعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما أرسلت «1» به، وإذا رأى مخيلة: قام وقعد، وجاء وذهب، وتغير لونه، فيقال له: يا رسول الله ما تخاف؟ فيقول: إنى أخاف أن يكون مثل قوم عاد حيث قالوا: «هذا عارض ممطرنا» .
Question
If you say: what is the benefit of ascribing the Lord to the wind?
فإن قلت: ما فائدة إضافة الرب إلى الريح؟
Answer
I say: it indicates that the wind and the turning of its reins are among what testifies to the greatness of His power, for it is among the wonders of His creation and the greatest of His soldiers. And mentioning the command, and its being commanded from Him, Almighty and Exalted, supports and strengthens that.
قلت: الدلالة على أن الريح وتصريف أعنتها مما يشهد لعظم قدرته، لأنها من أعاجيب خلقه وأكابر جنوده. وذكر الأمر وكونها مأمورة من جهته عز وجل: يعضد ذلك ويقوّيه،
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 307
1. (1) . The explanation of this verse-witness was given in this volume, page 12; consult it if you wish. — The corrector.
1. (1) . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بهذا الجزء صفحة 12 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
Vol. 4, p. 308
1. (1) . Recorded by Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Māja, al-Bazzār, Abū Yaʿlā, and by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad, all from the narration of ʿAṭāʾ from ʿĀʾisha; the wording of Muslim is close to the wording of the book.
2. . His saying “aghatha Abū l-Ṭayyib”: in the Ṣiḥāḥ, aghatha means “it was bad and corrupt”; one says: aghatha l-rajulu fī manṭiqihi (“the man was poor in his speech”). (ʿ)
3. . “By your life, what appeared of you to the striker is not deadlier / than what appeared of you to the faultfinder” — by Abū l-Ṭayyib. He says: By your life, what appeared of you to the striker, meaning the spearhead, is not more deadly, i.e., quicker to kill, than what appeared of you to the faultfinder, meaning the tongue; rather, they are equal in sharpness. It is also possible that he explicitly borrowed “killing” for “striking.”
4. . Aḥmad said: The verse of al-Mutanabbī is not as [al-Zamakhsharī] recited it; rather it is as it is transmitted: “laʿamruka inna mā bāna minka la-ḍāribun / bi-aqtala mimmā bāna minka li-ʿāʾibi.” It works only thus, because before it is: “He is the son of the Messenger of God and the son of His chosen one, / and their likeness was likened after trials” — from a qaṣīda in praise of Ṭāhir ibn al-Ḥusayn al-ʿAlawī. Had Abū l-Ṭayyib put “in” in place of “mā,” the verse would have been: “yarā anna inna mā bāna minka la-ḍāribun,” and this repetition is heavier than the repetition of “mā,” without doubt. Al-Zamakhsharī only found fault with him and bound him to use “in” in place of “mā” because he believed the verse to be as he recited it: “laʿamruka mā mā bāna minka li-ḍāribin / bi-aqtala mimmā bāna minka li-ʿāʾibi.” And had “in” replaced “mā,” as al-Zamakhsharī amended it, it would require the bāʾ to enter the predicate of “mā.” But the bāʾ enters only the predicate of the Ḥijāzī “mā” that operates; “in” does not operate the operation of “mā,” on the sound view, so the bāʾ cannot properly enter its predicate. Al-Mutanabbī did not depart from it except because it was impossible for him from every angle. Still, I do not absolve al-Mutanabbī of haughtiness, for he was fond of it, enamored of the unusual in composition. And al-Zamakhsharī relayed another view regarding the verse, namely making it a filler (ṣila), like it in the verse: “A man hopes for what he does not see, / and calamities intervene before its nearest part.” He said: “Its meaning on this view is: We established them in the like of what We established you in …” etc. I say: and specific to this group is His saying “And they said: Who is stronger than us in power? Did they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than them in power?” and His saying “We established them in the earth as We have not established you.”
1. (1) . أخرجه مسلم والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة والبزار وأبو يعلى والبخاري في الأدب المفرد، كلهم من رواية عطاء عن عائشة، ولفظ مسلم قريب من لفظ الكتاب.
2. . قوله «ولقد أغث أبو الطيب» في الصحاح «أغث» : أى ردؤ وفسد، تقول: أغث الرجل في منطقه. (ع) [.....]
3. . لعمرك ماما بان منك لضارب
…. بأقتل مما بان منك لعائب لأبى الطيب. يقول: وحياتك ليس الذي ظهر منك للضارب يعنى السنان، أفتل: أى أسرع قتلا من الذي ظهر منك للعائب، يعنى: اللسان، بل هما سواء في الحدة. ويجوز أنه استعار القتل للضرب تصريحا.
4. . قال أحمد: بيت المتنبي ليس كما أنشده، وإنما هو كما يروى: لعمرك إن ما بان منك لضارب
…. بأقتل مما بان منك لعائب ولا يستقيم إلا كذلك لأن قبله: هو ابن رسول الله وابن صفيه
…. وشبههما شبهت بعد التجارب من قصيدة يمدح بها طاهر بن الحسين العلوي، ولو أنى أبو الطيب عوض «ما» ب «إن» لجاء البيت: يرى أن إن ما بان منك لضارب وهذا التكرار أثقل من تكرار «ما» بلا مراء. وإنما فنده الزمخشري وألزمه استعمال «إن» عوض «ما» لاعتقاده أن البيت كما أنشده: لعمرك ما مابان منك لضارب
…. بأقتل مما بان منك لعائب ولو عوض «إن» عوض «ما» كما أصلحه الزمخشري: لزم دخول الباء في خبر «ما» وإنما تدخل الباء في خبر «ما» الحجازية العاملة، و «إن» لا تعمل عمل «ما» على الصحيح، فلا يستقيم دخول الباء في خبرها، فما عدل المتنبي عن ذلك إلا لتعذره عليه من كل وجه. على أنى لا أبرئ المتنبي من التعجرف، فانه كان مغرى به، مغرما بالغريب من النظم. ونقل الزمخشري في الآية وجها آخر: وهو جعلها صلة مثلها في قوله: يرجى المرء ما إن لا يراه
…. وتعرض دون أدناه الخطوب قال: ويكون معناه على هذا مكناهم في مثل ما مكناكم
…. الخ» قلت: واختص بهذه الطائفة قوله تعالى وَقالُوا مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وقوله مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ ما لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ.

Q 46:26 · Vol. 4, pp. 308–310

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And We had certainly established them in what We have not established you in, and We made for them hearing, sight and hearts; but their hearing, their sight and their hearts availed them nothing, since they used to reject God’s signs, and that which they used to mock at enveloped them (26)
وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيما إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِذْ كانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ (26)
Vol. 4, p. 308
“in” (in) is a negative, i.e., “in what We have not established you in”; but “in” is better in expression, because of the combining of “mā” with its like, an offensive repetition. Like it, [such repetition] is avoided: do you not see that the origin of “mahmā” is “mā mā,” and because of the ugliness of the repetition they turned the first alif into hāʾ. And Abū l-Ṭayyib was indeed poor(2) in his saying: “By your life, mā mā bāna minka li-ḍāribin”(3) — what would it have cost him to follow the sweetness of the wording of the Revelation and say: “By your life, mā in bāna minka li-ḍāribin”?(4)
إِنْ نافية، أى: فيما ما مكنا كم فيه، إلا أنّ إِنْ أحسن في اللفظ، لما فيه مجامعة ما مثلها من التكرير المستبشع. ومثله مجتنب، ألا ترى أن الأصل في «مهما» : «ماماز» لبشاعة التكرير: قلبوا الألف هاء. ولقد أغث «2» أبو الطيب في قوله: لعمرك ماما بان منك لضارب «3» وما ضره لو اقتدى بعذوبة لفظ التنزيل فقال: لعمرك ما إن بان منك لضارب «4»
Vol. 4, p. 309
and “in” was made a filler (ṣila), like it in what al-Akhfash recited: “A man hopes for what he does not see, and calamities intervene short of its nearest part”(1) — and it is interpreted as “We established them in the like of what We established you in.” The first view is the sound one, and on it more than one verse of the Qur’an has come: “they were better in furnishings and appearance”; “they were more numerous than them and stronger in power and in traces.” It is more effective in rebuke and more effective in urging reflection. “of anything”: i.e., of any availing, and it is the little of it.
وقد جعلت إن صلة، مثلها فيما أنشده الأخفش: يرجّى المرء ما إن لا يراه … وتعرض دون أدناه الخطوب «1» وتؤوّل بإنا مكناهم في مثل ما مكناكم فيه: والوجه هو الأوّل، ولقد جاء عليه غير آية في القرآن هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثاثاً وَرِءْياً، كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَآثاراً وهو أبلغ في التوبيخ، وأدخل في الحث على الاعتبار مِنْ شَيْءٍ أى من شيء من الإغناء، وهو القليل منه.
Question
If you say: what governs “idh kānū yajḥadūn”?
فإن قلت بم انتصب إِذْ كانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ؟
Answer
I say: His saying “fa-mā aghnā.”
قلت: بقوله تعالى فَما أَغْنى.
Question
If you say: why does it work as a causal clause?
فإن قلت: لم جرى مجرى التعليل؟
Answer
I say: because the import of the causal clause and the adverbial is equal in your saying “I hit him for his bad conduct” and “I hit him when he misbehaved.” For if you hit him at the time of his misbehavior, you hit him then only because of the existence of his misbehavior then; but “idh” and “ḥaythu” prevail over the other adverbials in that.
قلت: لاستواء مؤدى التعليل والظرف في قولك: ضربته لإساءته وضربته إذا أساء، لأنك إذا ضربته في وقت إساءته، فإنما ضربته فيه لوجود إساءته فيه، إلا أن «إذ، وحيث، غلبتا دون سائر الظروف في ذلك.
Vol. 4, p. 310

Vol. 4, p. 309
1. (1) . “If I hold back, then life is sweet … to [me], as though it were mixed honey. / A man hopes for what he does not see, and calamities intervene before its nearest part. / And the eager one does not know on what his sharāshir will fall, / whether he will err or hit” — by Jābir ibn Rālān al-Ṭāʾī. It is said: by Iyās ibn al-Arat. Al-sharāshir: plural of sharshar, which are the extremities of a thing that are scattered and spread out; it is applied to the body and to weight and is used figuratively for the self, as here. It is said: they are hunting nets. He says: if I am miserly, life is sweet to him like the sweetness of honey mixed with water so that its heat is removed; and he implied in “sweet” the sense of “beloved,” so he made it transitive with “ilā.” Then he said: but there is no good in withholding, for a man hopes for the matter absent from him, while the terrors of death or the hardships of time intervene between him and the nearest thing of it. And “in” is redundant after the relative “mā,” by analogy with the negative “mā.” And the eager one, who has turned his whole self toward the world, does not know the outcomes of his affair, whether he will gain or lose. On the interpretation of sharāshir as hunting nets, there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), in that he likens the state of one who engages in the means of a matter, ignorant of its outcome, to the state of one who sets nets for hunting, “fa-qad wa-qad” [the source text breaks off here].
1. (1) . فان أمسك فان العيش حلو
…. إلى كأنه عسل مشوب يرجي المرء ما إن لا يراه
…. وتعرض دون أدناه الخطوب وما يدرى الحريص علام يلقى
…. شراشره أيخطئ أم يصيب لجابر بن رالان الطائي. وقيل: لا ياس بن الأرت. والشراشر: جمع شرشر، وهي أطراف الشيء المشرشرة، أى: المفرقة المنشورة، وتطلق على الجسد وعلى الثقل ويكنى بها عن النفس كما هنا. وقيل: هي حبال الصيد. يقول: إن أبخل فالعيش حلو عنده كحلاوة العسل الممزوج بالماء لتزول حرارته وضمن «حلو» معنى محبوب، فعداء بإلى. ثم قال: ولكن لا خير في الإمساك، فان المرء يرتجى الأمر الغائب عنه. وتحول أهوال الموت أو شدائد الدهر بينه وبين أدنى شيء منه. وإن: زائدة بعد ما الموصولة حملا على ما النافية، وما يدرى الذي وجه نفسه بكليتها للدنيا عواقب أمره، أريح أم خسر، وعلى أنها حبال الصيد ففي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية حيث شبه حال من أخذ في أسباب الأمر جاهلا عاقبته: بحال من نصب الحبال للصيد، فقد وقد.
Vol. 4, p. 310
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “One of the two objects of ittakhadha, the one that returns to the relative, is omitted … etc.” Aḥmad said: The reason for the corruption of meaning on this analysis is not clear. We make it clear and say: if “qurbānan” were a second object, with the meaning “as a means of drawing near by them,” the meaning would come to this: that they were rebuked for abandoning the taking of God as that by which one draws near. For when a master rebukes his slave and says, “You took so-and-so as lord instead of me,” its meaning is blame for attributing lordship to another; and this is not the aim here, for God is the one drawn near to, and none else is drawn near by Him to another. Rather, the rebuke fell on attributing divinity to other than God Most High; so the proper structure of the speech is that “ālihatan” alone is the second object.
2. . His saying “ittakhadha, the one returning to ‘alladhīna,’ the omitted”: it is that which he made explicit in his saying: “i.e., ittakhadhūhum” [“they took them”]. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «أحد مفعولي اتخذ الراجع إلى الموصول محذوف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لم يتبين وجه فساد المعنى على هذا الاعراب. ونحن نبينه فنقول: لو كان قربانا مفعولا ثانيا ومعناه متقربا بهم: لصار المعنى إلى أنهم وبخوا على ترك اتخاذ الله متقربا به، لأن السيد إذا ونخ عبده وقال: اتخذت فلانا سيدا دوني، فإنما معناه اللوم على نسبة السيادة إلى غيره، وليس هذا المقصد، فان الله تعالى يتقرب إليه ولا يتقرب به لغيره، فإنما وقع التوبيخ على نسبة الالهية إلى غير الله تعالى، فكان حق الكلام أن يكون آلهة هو المفعول الثاني لا غير.
2. . قوله «اتخذ الراجع إلى الذين المحذوف» هو الذي أبرزه في قوله: أى اتخذوهم. (ع)

Q 46:27 · Vol. 4, p. 310

Verse 27

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And We have indeed destroyed the towns around you, and We diversified the signs that perhaps they would return (27)
وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا ما حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرى وَصَرَّفْنَا الْآياتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (27)
Vol. 4, p. 310
“what is around you,” O people of Mecca, “of the towns”: such as the Ḥijr of Thamūd, the town of Sodom, and others. What is meant is the people of the towns; hence He said “that perhaps they would return.”
ما حَوْلَكُمْ يا أهل مكة مِنَ الْقُرى من نحو حجر ثمود وقرية سدوم وغيرهما. والمراد: أهل القرى. ولذلك قال لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 310
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “One of the two objects of ittakhadha, the one that returns to the relative, is omitted … etc.” Aḥmad said: The reason for the corruption of meaning on this analysis is not clear. We make it clear and say: if “qurbānan” were a second object, with the meaning “as a means of drawing near by them,” the meaning would come to this: that they were rebuked for abandoning the taking of God as that by which one draws near. For when a master rebukes his slave and says, “You took so-and-so as lord instead of me,” its meaning is blame for attributing lordship to another; and this is not the aim here, for God is the one drawn near to, and none else is drawn near by Him to another. Rather, the rebuke fell on attributing divinity to other than God Most High; so the proper structure of the speech is that “ālihatan” alone is the second object.
2. . His saying “ittakhadha, the one returning to ‘alladhīna,’ the omitted”: it is that which he made explicit in his saying: “i.e., ittakhadhūhum” [“they took them”]. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «أحد مفعولي اتخذ الراجع إلى الموصول محذوف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لم يتبين وجه فساد المعنى على هذا الاعراب. ونحن نبينه فنقول: لو كان قربانا مفعولا ثانيا ومعناه متقربا بهم: لصار المعنى إلى أنهم وبخوا على ترك اتخاذ الله متقربا به، لأن السيد إذا ونخ عبده وقال: اتخذت فلانا سيدا دوني، فإنما معناه اللوم على نسبة السيادة إلى غيره، وليس هذا المقصد، فان الله تعالى يتقرب إليه ولا يتقرب به لغيره، فإنما وقع التوبيخ على نسبة الالهية إلى غير الله تعالى، فكان حق الكلام أن يكون آلهة هو المفعول الثاني لا غير.
2. . قوله «اتخذ الراجع إلى الذين المحذوف» هو الذي أبرزه في قوله: أى اتخذوهم. (ع)
20
Q 46:28 · Vol. 4, p. 310

Verse 28

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Then why did those not help them whom they had taken, besides God, as gods by which to draw near [to Him]? Rather, they were lost to them; and that was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate (28)
فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (28)
Vol. 4, p. 310
Al-qurbān is that by which one draws near to God Most High; i.e., they took them as intercessors, as a means of drawing near by them to God, in that they said: “These are our intercessors with God.” One of the two objects of ittakhadha, namely the one that returns to the relative pronoun “alladhīna,”(1) is omitted,(2) and the second is “ālihatan.” And “qurbānan” is a ḥāl. It is not valid for “qurbānan” to be the second object with “ālihatan” an apposition to it, because of the corruption of the meaning. It is also read “qurubānan” with ḍamma on the rāʾ. The meaning: then why did their gods not prevent their destruction? “Rather, they were lost to them”: absent from helping them. “And that” points to the refusal of their gods’ help to them and their straying from them; i.e., “that” is the effect of their ifk, which is their taking them as gods, and the fruit of their polytheism and of their fabricating falsehood against God in His being possessed of partners. It is also read “afkuhum” [“ifkuhum” and “afkuhum”]; al-afk and al-ifk are like al-ḥadhar and al-ḥidhr. It is read “wa-dhālika ifkuhum,” i.e., that taking, whose effect and fruit this is, was their turning away from the truth. It is read “affakahum,” with tashdīd for emphasis; and “āfakahum”: He made them turners-away (āfikīn). And “āfikuhum,” i.e., their lying speech, “possessor of ifk,” as you say “qawl kādhib” (“a liar’s speech”). “And that is of the ifk of what they used to fabricate,” i.e., part of the falsehood they used to fabricate.
القربان: ما تقرب به إلى الله تعالى، أى: اتخذوهم شفعاء متقربا بهم إلى الله، حيث قالوا: هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله. وأحد مفعولي اتخذ الراجع إلى الذين «1» المحذوف «2» ، والثاني: آلهة. وقربانا: حال ولا يصح أن يكون قربانا مفعولا ثانيا وآلهة بدلا منه لفساد المعنى. وقرئ قربانا بضم الراء. والمعنى: فهلا منعهم من الهلاك آلهتهم بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ أى غابوا عن نصرتهم وَذلِكَ إشارة إلى امتناع نصرة آلهتهم لهم وضلالهم عنهم، أى: وذلك أثر إفكهم الذي هو اتخاذهم إياها آلهة، وثمرة شركهم وافترائهم على الله الكذب من كونه ذا شركاء. وقرئ: إفكهم: والأفك والإفك: كالحذر والحذر. وقرئ: وذلك إفكهم، أى: وذلك الاتخاذ الذي هذا أثره وثمرته صرفهم عن الحق. وقرئ: أفكهم على التشديد للمبالغة. وآفكهم: جعلهم آفكين. وآفكهم، أى: قولهم الآفك ذو الإفك، كما تقول قول كاذب، وذلك إفك مما كانوا يفترون، أى: بعض ما كانوا يفترون من الإفك.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 310

Q 46:29–32 · Vol. 4, pp. 310–313

Verses 29 to 32

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And when We directed to you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an; and when they attended it, they said: “Be silent.” And when it was concluded, they turned back to their people as warners (29) They said: “O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path (30) O our people, respond to God’s caller and believe in Him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment (31) And whoever does not respond to God’s caller will not be able to escape in the earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error” (32)
وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا أَنْصِتُوا فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوْا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ (29) قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا كِتاباً أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ وَإِلى طَرِيقٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (30) يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُجِرْكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ (31) وَمَنْ لا يُجِبْ داعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءُ أُولئِكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ (32)
Vol. 4, p. 311
“We directed to you a group”: We turned them toward you and brought them to you. It is also read “ṣarrafnā” with tashdīd, because they were a number. Al-nafar: fewer than ten. It is pluralized as anfār. In the ḥadīth of Abū Dharr ؓ: “If only one of our anfār were here.”(1) “when they attended it”: the pronoun refers to the Qur’an, i.e., when it was within their hearing; or to the Messenger of God ﷺ supported by the reading of one who read “fa-lammā quḍiya,” i.e., when he completed his recitation and finished it. “they said”: some said to others “Anṣitū,” i.e., be silent, listening. One says: anṣata li-kadhā and istanṣata lahu. It is related that the jinn used to eavesdrop, and when the sky was guarded and they were pelted with shooting stars, they said: “This can only be on account of some news that has occurred.” So seven or nine persons of the nobles of the jinn of Naṣībīn or Nīnawā rose — among them Zawbaʿa — and struck out until they reached Tihāma, then rushed to the valley of Nakhla, where they met(2) the Messenger of God ﷺ standing in the depth of the night praying, or in the dawn prayer, and they listened to his recitation. That was upon his return from al-Ṭāʾif, when he had gone out to them seeking their support and they did not respond to his request and incited the fools of Thaqīf against him.(3) From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr ؓ: the Messenger of God ﷺ did not recite to the jinn and did not see them; he was only reciting in his prayer, and they passed by him and stopped, listening, without his being aware, and God informed him of their listening.(4) It is said: rather, God commanded His Messenger to warn the jinn and to recite to them, and He directed to him a group of them, gathering them for him. So he said: “I have been commanded to recite to the jinn tonight; who will follow me?” — he said it three times — and they lowered their heads, except ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd ؓ who said: “None attended him on the night of the jinn other than I. So we set off until, when we were at the top of Mecca in the pass of al-Ḥajūn, he drew a line for me and said: ‘Do not go out of it until I return to you.’ Then he began the Qur’an, and I heard a tremendous clamor, until I feared
صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً أملناهم إليك وأقبلنا بهم نحوك. وقرئ: صرفنا بالتشديد، لأنهم جماعة. والنفر: دون العشرة. ويجمع أنفارا. وفي حديث أبى ذر رضى الله عنه: لو كان هاهنا أحد من أنفارنا «1» فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ الضمير للقرآن. أى: فلما كان بمسمع منهم. أو لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. وتعضده قراءة من قرأ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ أى أتمّ قراءته وفرع منها قالُوا قال بعضهم لبعض أَنْصِتُوا اسكتوا مستمعين. يقال: أنصت لكذا واستنصت له. روى أنّ الجنّ كانت تسترق السمع، فلما حرست السماء ورجموا بالشهب قالوا: ما هذا إلا لنبإ حدث، فنهض سبعة نفر أو تسعة من أشراف جنّ نصيبين أو نينوى: منهم زوبعة، فضربوا حتى بلغوا تهامة، ثم اندفعوا إلى وادى نخلة، فوافقوا «2» رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو قائم في جوف الليل يصلى أو في صلاة الفجر، فاستمعوا لقراءته، وذلك عند منصرفه من الطائف حين خرج إليهم يستنصرهم فلم يجيبوه إلى طلبته وأغروا به سفهاء ثقيف «3» . وعن سعيد بن جبير رضى الله عنه: ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن ولا رآهم، وإنما كان يتلو في صلاته فمروا به فوقفوا مستمعين وهو لا يشعر، فأنبأه الله باستماعهم «4» . وقيل: بل أمر الله رسوله أن ينذر الجنّ ويقرأ عليهم فصرف إليه نفرا منهم جمعهم له فقال: إنى أمرت أن أقرأ على الجنّ الليلة فمن يتبعني: قالها ثلاثا، فأطرقوا إلا عبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله عنه قال: لم يحضره ليلة الجنّ أحد غيرى، فانطلقنا حتى إذا كنا بأعلى مكة في شعب الحجون فخط لي خطا وقال: لا تخرج منه حتى أعود إليك، ثم افتتح القرآن وسمعت لغطا شديدا حتى خفت
Vol. 4, p. 312
for the Messenger of God ﷺ; and many dark forms covered him, coming between me and him until I could not hear his voice; then they dispersed as clouds disperse. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: ‘Did you see anything?’ I said: ‘Yes, black men wrapped in white garments (mustathfirī).’(1) He said: ‘Those are the jinn of Naṣībīn.’”(2) They were twelve thousand, and the sūra he recited to them was “Read in the name of your Lord.”
على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وغشيته أسودة كثيرة حالت بيني وبينه حتى ما أسمع صوته ثم انقطعوا كقطع السحاب فقال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هل رأيت شيئا؟ قلت: نعم رجالا سودا مستثفري ثياب بيض «1» ، فقال: أولئك جنّ نصيبين» «2» وكانوا اثنى عشر ألفا، والسورة التي قرأها عليهم اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ.
Question
If you say: how could they say “after Moses”?
فإن قلت: كيف قالوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى؟
Answer
I say: from ʿAṭāʾ ؓ: that they were Jews. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both: the jinn had not heard of the matter of ʿĪsā (Jesus) ﷺ; therefore they said “after Moses.”
قلت: عن عطاء رضى الله عنه: أنهم كانوا على اليهودية. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: إنّ الجنّ لم تكن سمعت بأمر عيسى عليه السلام، فلذلك قالت: من بعد موسى.
Question
If you say: why was it made partial in “min dhunūbikum” (“some of your sins”)?
فإن قلت: لم بعّض في قوله مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ؟
Answer
I say: because among sins are some that are not forgiven by faith, such as sins of wrongs done to others (maẓālim)(3) and the like. Like it is His saying: “[Say:] Worship God and fear Him and obey me; He will forgive you some of your sins.”
قلت: لأن من الذنوب ما لا يغفر بالإيمان كذنوب المظالم «3» ونحوها. ونحوه قوله عز وجل أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ.
Question
If you say: do the jinn have a reward as humans do?
فإن قلت: هل للجنّ ثواب كما للإنس؟
Answer
I say: it is disputed. It is said: they have no reward except salvation from the Fire, because of His saying “and protect you from a painful punishment,” and Abū Ḥanīfa ؒ used to incline to this. The sound view is that they are in the same ruling as the children of Adam, because they are legally responsible like them. “Then he is not one who can escape in the earth”: i.e., no flight saves from Him, and no one who outstrips can outstrip His decree. Similar is His saying: “And we thought that we would never be able to escape God in the earth, nor to escape Him by flight.”
قلت: اختلف فيه فقيل: لا ثواب لهم إلا النجاة من النار، لقوله تعالى وَيُجِرْكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ وإليه كان يذهب أبو حنيفة رحمه الله. والصحيح أنهم في حكم بنى آدم، لأنهم مكلفون مثلهم فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ أى: لا ينجى منه مهرب، ولا يسبق قضاءه سابق. ونحوه قوله تعالى وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ هَرَباً.
Vol. 4, p. 313

Vol. 4, p. 311
1. (1) . This is a portion of the story of Abū Dharr’s conversion, from the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣāmit from Abū Dharr, mentioned at length. In it: “While I was on a moonlit night [the printed word is garbled], and God had cast sleep upon the people of Mecca so that none was circumambulating but two women, they came to me” — and he mentioned the story. In it: “Then they went off wailing and saying: ‘If only one of our anṣār [helpers] were here.’” Muslim recorded it at length.
2. . His saying “fa-wāfaqū rasūl Allāh”: perhaps [it should read] “fa-wāfaw.” (ʿ)
3. . Agreed upon in meaning from the narration of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, except for its beginning; and except for the statement “and they were nine persons, one of whom was Zawbaʿa”; and except for “in the depth of the night praying”; and except for “from Nīnawā”; and except for “upon his return” to the end. As for Zawbaʿa, al-Ḥākim recorded it from the narration of Dharr from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “They descended — meaning the jinn — upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting the Qur’an in the valley of Nakhla. When they heard it they said ‘Be silent’; and they were nine, one of whom was Zawbaʿa. So God revealed ‘And when We directed to you …’” — the verse. As for “Nīnawā,” al-Ṭabarī recorded it from the narration of Qatāda on this verse; he said: “It was mentioned to us that they were directed to him from Nīnawā” — the ḥadīth.
4. . Agreed upon from the narration of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and it is within the preceding [report].
1. (1) . هذا طرف من قصة إسلام أبى ذر رضى الله عنه من رواية عبد الله بن الصامت عن أبى ذر ذكره مطولا. وفيه: فبينا أنا في ليلة قمراء ختموانية وقد ضرب الله على أهل مكة فما يطوف غير امرأتين، فأتيا على فذكر القصة. وفيه ثم انطلقتا يولولان. ويقولان لو كان هاهنا أحد من أنصارنا» أخرجه مسلم مطولا.
2. . قوله «فوافقوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم» لعله: فوافوا. (ع)
3. . متفق عليه بمعناه من رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس دون أوله. ودون قوله «وكانوا تسعة نفر أحدهم زوبعة» ودون قوله «في جوف الليل يصلى» ودون قوله «من نينوى» ودون قوله «عند منصرفه إلى آخره» وأما زوبعة فأخرجه الحاكم من رواية ذر عن ابن مسعود قال «هبطوا- يعنى الجن- على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ القرآن ببطن نخلة. فلما سمعوه قالوا أنصتوا. وكانوا تسعة أحدهم زوبعة. فأنزل الله وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ- الآية وقوله «نينوى» أخرجه الطبري من رواية قتادة في هذه الآية قال: ذكر لنا أنهم صرفوا إليه من نينوى الحديث» .
4. . متفق عليه من رواية سعيد بن جبير، وهو في الذي قبله.
Vol. 4, p. 312
1. (1) . His saying “mustathfirī thiyāb bīḍ”: in al-Qāmūs, al-istithfār is to put one’s waist-wrapper, twisted, between one’s thighs; and a dog’s putting its tail between its thighs until it sticks to its belly. (ʿ)
2. . I did not find it complete in a single context; rather I found it scattered. Al-Ṭabarī narrated from the narration of Qatāda: “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘I have been commanded to recite to the jinn; which of you will follow me?’ They lowered their heads three times, except Ibn Masʿūd, who followed him until he entered a pass called the pass of al-Ḥajūn.” He said: “And he drew a line around Ibn Masʿūd” — then he mentioned [the passage], i.e., his saying “until I feared for him,” and added in it: “I said: ‘What is this clamor?’ He said: ‘They disputed before me concerning a mountain; I judged between them with the truth.’” Al-Ḥākim, al-Ṭabarānī and al-Dāraquṭnī narrated from the route of Abū ʿUthmān ibn Shayba al-Khuzāʿī, a man of the people of al-Shām, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd say: “The Messenger of God ﷺ said to his companions while he was in Mecca: ‘Whoever of you would like to attend the matter of the jinn tonight, let him do so.’ None of them attended except me. He said: I set out until, when we were at the top of Mecca, he drew a line for me with his foot, then commanded me to sit in it, then went on until he stood. He began the Qur’an” — the ḥadīth — and he did not mention the saying “black men …” to the end. Al-Ṭabarī narrated from the narration of ʿAmr ibn Ghaylān al-Thaqafī that he asked Ibn Masʿūd, who mentioned the story. In it: “[He said:] ‘Did you see anything?’ I said: ‘Yes, I saw black men wrapped (mustashʿirīn) in white garments.’ He said: ‘Those are the jinn of Naṣībīn; they asked me for provisions’” — and he mentioned the ḥadīth — and it contains neither their number nor the name of the sūra. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from the narration of ʿIkrima on this verse: “They were of the jinn of Naṣībīn; they came from the island of al-Mawṣil. And they were twelve thousand.” So all that he [al-Zamakhsharī] mentioned is found in the totality of these ḥadīths, except the name of the sūra.
3. . Maḥmūd said: “He made the forgiveness partial because among sins are some that faith does not forgive, such as sins of wrongs.” Aḥmad said: What he stated absolutely, that faith does not forgive wrongs, is not correct. For if a ḥarbī [a non-Muslim belligerent] had plundered protected property and shed protected blood and then his Islam were good, Islam would cut off from him the sin of what preceded, without difficulty. It is said: God did not promise forgiveness to the disbeliever on condition of faith, in the Book of God Most High, except in a partial form, and this is one such case. If there is no secret in its being consistent in that way, it is only that the disbeliever’s station is one of contraction (qabḍ), not of expansion (basṭ), and so He did not expand his hope for the forgiveness of all sins. The like of this has also come frequently in the case of believers. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قوله «مستثفري ثياب بيض» في القاموس «الاستئفار» : أن يدخل إزاره بين فخذيه ملويا وإدخال الكلب ذنبه بين فخذيه حتى يلزقه ببطنه اه (ع)
2. . لم أجده بتمامه في سياق واحد. بل وجدته مفرقا. فروى الطبري من رواية قتادة ذكر لنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال «إنى أمرت أن أقرأ على الجن. فأيكم يتبعني فأطرقوا ثلاثا إلا ابن مسعود قاتبعه حتى دخل شعبا يقال له شعب الحجون قال: وخط على ابن مسعود خطا. فذكر أى قوله حتى خفت عليه- وزاد فيه: فقلت ما هذا اللغط؟ فقال: اختصموا إلى في جبل قضيت بينهم بالحق» وروى الحاكم والطبراني والدارقطني من طريق أبى عثمان ابن شيبة الخزاعي وكان رجلا من أهل الشام أنه سمع عبد الله بن مسعود يقول «إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه وهو بمكة: من أحب منكم أن يحضر الليلة أمر الجن فليفعل. فلم يحضر منهم أحد غيرى. قال: فانطلقت حتى إذا كنا بأعلى مكة خط لي برجله خطا ثم أمرنى أن أجلس فيه، ثم انطلق حتى قام. فافتتح القرآن- الحديث» ولم يذكر قوله «رجالا سودا إلى آخره» وروى الطبري من رواية عمرو بن غيلان الثقفي أنه سأل ابن مسعود فذكر القصة. وفيها فقال «رأيت شيئا؟ قلت: نعم. قد رأيت رجالا سودا مستشعرين بثياب بيض. فقال: أولئك جن نصيبين سألونى المتاع- فذكر الحديث» وليس فيه عددهم ولا اسم السورة. وروى ابن أبى حاتم من رواية عكرمة في هذه الآية قال «كانوا من جن نصيبين جاءوا من جزيرة الموصل. وكانوا اثنى عشر ألفا» فهذه الأحاديث من مجموعها ما ذكر إلا اسم السورة.
3. . قال محمود: «إنما بعض المغفرة لأن من الذنوب مالا يغفره الايمان كذنوب المظالم» قال أحمد: ليس ما أطلقه من أن الايمان لا يغفر المظالم بصحيح، لأن الحربي لو نهب الأموال المصونة وسفك الدماء المحقونة ثم حسن إسلامه: جب الإسلام عنه إثم ما تقدم بلا إشكال. ويقال: إنه ما وعد المغفرة الكافر على تقدير الايمان في كتاب الله تعالى إلا مبعضة، وهذا منه، فان لم يكن لاطراده بذلك سر فما هو إلا أن مقام الكافر قبض لا بسط، فلذلك لم يبسط رجاءه في مغفرة جملة الذنوب. وقد ورد في حق المؤمنين مثله كثيرا، والله أعلم.
22
Q 46:33 · Vol. 4, p. 313

Verse 33

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes! Indeed He is competent over all things (33)
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى بَلى إِنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (33)
Vol. 4, p. 313
“bi-qādirin”: its position is nominative, because it is the predicate of “anna”; this is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: “qādirun.” The bāʾ entered only because the negation at the beginning of the verse covers “anna” and what is within its scope. Al-Zajjāj said: if you said “mā ẓanantu anna Zaydan bi-qāʾimin,” it would be permissible, as though it were said: “Is not God able?” Do you not see the occurrence of “yes” (balā) confirming power over all things, of resurrection and otherwise, and not [confirming] their seeing? It is also read “yaqdiru.” One says: ʿayītu bi-l-amr, when you did not know the way to it; from it: “Were We wearied by the first creation?”
بِقادِرٍ محله الرفع، لأنه خبر أن، يدل عليه قراءة عبد الله: قادر، وإنما دخلت الباء لاشتمال النفي في أوّل الآية على أن وما في حيزها. وقال الزجاج: لو قلت: ما ظننت أنّ زيدا بقائم: جاز، كأنه قيل: أليس الله بقادر. ألا ترى إلى وقوع بلى مقرّرة للقدرة على كل شيء من البعث وغيره، لا لرؤيتهم. وقرئ: يقدر. ويقال: عييت بالأمر، إذا لم تعرف وجهه. ومنه أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ.
23
Q 46:34 · Vol. 4, p. 313

Verse 34

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: “Is this not the truth?” They will say: “Yes, by our Lord.” He will say: “Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve” (34)
وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَلَيْسَ هذا بِالْحَقِّ قالُوا بَلى وَرَبِّنا قالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ (34)
Vol. 4, p. 313
“Is this not the truth?” is quoted following an implied saying, and this implied saying is the operator of the adverbial. “This” points to the punishment, as shown by His saying “taste the punishment.” The meaning is mockery of them and rebuke of them for their ridiculing God’s promise and threat, and for their saying “and we are not to be punished.”
أَلَيْسَ هذا بِالْحَقِّ محكي بعد قول مضمر، وهذا المضمر هو ناصب الظرف. وهذا إشارة إلى العذاب، بدليل قوله تعالى فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ والمعنى: التهكم بهم، والتوبيخ لهم على استهزائهم بوعد الله ووعيده، وقولهم وَما نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ.
24
Q 46:35 · Vol. 4, pp. 313–314

Verse 35

The verse as the commentary quotes it
So be patient, as the messengers of firm resolve were patient, and do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them. On the Day they see what they are promised, it will be as though they had not remained except an hour of a day. [This is] a notification. So will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people? (35)
فَاصْبِرْ كَما صَبَرَ أُولُوا الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ما يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلاَّ ساعَةً مِنْ نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلاَّ الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ (35)
Vol. 4, p. 313
“Ulū l-ʿazm”: those of earnestness, steadfastness and patience. And “min” may be partitive, in which case ulū l-ʿazm means some of the prophets. It is said: they are Noah, who was patient with harm from his people — they used to beat him until he lost consciousness; Abraham, with regard to the fire and the slaughter of his son; Isaac, with regard to the slaughter; Jacob, with regard to the loss of his son and the loss of his sight; Joseph, with regard to the well and the prison; Job, with regard to affliction; Moses, to whom his people said “We are about to be overtaken,” and he said “No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me”; David, who wept over his error for forty years; and Jesus, who did not lay a brick upon a brick and said: “It is a crossing-place, so cross it and do not build it up.” And God said of Adam “and We did not find in him resolve,” and of Jonah “and do not be like the companion of the whale.” It is also possible that “min” is explanatory, so that ulū l-ʿazm is a description of all the messengers. “And do not seek to hasten” punishment for the unbelievers of Quraysh, i.e., do not pray for its hastening, for it will surely descend upon them, even if delayed; and they will then consider short the duration of their stay in the world, to the point that they reckon it “an hour of a day.” “A notification” (balāgh)
أُولُوا الْعَزْمِ أولوا الجد والثبات والصبر. ومِنَ يجوز أن تكون للتبعيض، ويراد بأولى العزم: بعض الأنبياء. قيل: هم نوح، صبر على أذى قومه: كانوا يضربونه حتى يغشى عليه، وإبراهيم على النار وذبح ولده، وإسحاق على الذبح، ويعقوب على فقد ولده وذهاب بصره، ويوسف على الجب والسجن، وأيوب على الضرّ، وموسى قال له قومه: إنا لمدركون، قال: كلا إنّ معى ربى سيهدين، وداود بكى على خطيئته أربعين سنة، وعيسى لم يضع لبنة على لبنة وقال: إنها معبرة فاعبروها ولا تعمروها. وقال الله تعالى في آدم وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً وفي يونس وَلا تَكُنْ كَصاحِبِ الْحُوتِ ويجوز أن تكون للبيان، فيكون أولو العزم صفة الرسل كلهم وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لكفار قريش بالعذاب، أى: لا تدع لهم بتعجيله، فإنه نازل بهم لا محالة، وإن تأخر، وأنهم مستقصرون حينئذ مدّة لبثهم في الدنيا حتى يحسبوها ساعَةً مِنْ نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ
Vol. 4, p. 314
i.e., this with which you have been admonished is sufficient in admonition; or this is a delivery of the message from the Messenger ﷺ. “Will any be destroyed except” those who depart from taking admonition from it and from acting upon what it requires? The sense of delivery is indicated by the reading of one who read “ballagha; fa-hal yuhlaku”; and it is read “balāghan,” i.e., “deliver a delivery”; and it is read “yuhlaku,” with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with kasra or fatḥa on the lām, from halaka and halika; and “nuhliku,” with nūn. “except the defiantly disobedient people.” From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Whoever recites Sūrat al-Aḥqāf will have ten good deeds recorded for him for every grain of sand in the world.”(1)
أى هذا الذي وعظتم به كفاية في الموعظة. أو هذا تبليغ من الرسول عليه السلام فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إلا الخارجون عن الاتعاظ به، والعمل بموجبه. ويدل على معنى التبليغ قراءة من قرأ: بلغ فهل يهلك: وقرئ: بلاغا، أى بلغوا بلاغا: وقرئ: يهلك، بفتح الياء وكسر اللام وفتحها، من هلك وهلك. ونهلك بالنون إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة الأحقاف كتب له عشر حسنات بعدد كل رملة في الدنيا» «1» .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 314
1. (1) . Recorded by al-Thaʿlabī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wāḥidī, with their chains of transmission, to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ؓ.
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي وابن مردويه والواحدي بأسانيدهم إلى أبى بن كعب رضى الله عنه.
